exposure: cervical stiffness ratio (measured via tension elastography)
cohort: A total of 50 nulliparous women in late pregnancy undergoing labor induction were included, 43 of whom had vaginal delivery and 7 underwent cesarean section.
finding: Cervical length and stiffness ratio, assessed via strain elastography before induction, showed no significant predictive value for induction of labor success.
mod_finding: While 43 women had vaginal delivery and 7 underwent cesarean section, cervical length and stiffness ratio were not found to significantly predict successful labor induction, which influences the mode of birth.
